A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S5 compression and Loihi 2 deployment study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendix A are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio-denoising experiments, sparsity and quantization analyses, and measured Loihi 2 versus Jetson performance, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds keyword-spotting results and measurements of energy and latency across batch sizes.

M1.justification: The S5 architecture, iterative pruning, ReLU-fication, W8A16 quantization, and per-sequence inference remain unchanged. The added batching experiment replicates existing models across hardware resources; keyword spotting reuses the existing scaling protocol.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates audio denoising on Intel N-DNS. v2 additionally evaluates SpeechCommands V2-35 keyword spotting in Appendix A.3.1 and Figure 9, extending coverage to speech classification. The batching experiment retains the denoising task rather than establishing a new microphone-data scenario.

E2.justification: The dense S5, Spiking-FullSubNet-XL, and Jetson Orin Nano comparisons are retained. Keyword spotting extends the existing dense-versus-sparse S5 comparison, and the batching sweep retains the Loihi-versus-Jetson comparator pair.

E3.justification: v2 adds a batch-size sweep from 1 to 16 using replicated models on a 16-chip Loihi 2 VPX board, plus accuracy-versus-compute evaluation for keyword spotting. These extend the evaluation settings; the original denoising splits, preprocessing, training recipe, and Table 1 protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 tests how batch size affects hardware energy efficiency and latency. The existing weight/activation sparsity, quantization, execution-mode, and fixed-point mismatch analyses are retained. The keyword-spotting benchmark adds coverage rather than a separate ablation.

E5.justification: Table 1 still averages measurements over eight random test samples, and the existing layerwise mismatch summaries are retained. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds a keyword-spotting accuracy/compute frontier and a hardware batching result series. Section 3.3 reports 4.43–4.72× lower energy per sample and 4.52× lower average latency for Loihi in the new sweep. These expand the results substantially; the original Figure 4 and Table 1 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The recurrent equations, pruning and quantization formulas, real-time power calculation, and Appendix A.1 MAC derivations retain their mathematical substance. Neither version adds a new theorem or proof relative to the other.

C1.justification: The four research questions and headline claims remain: sparse-model efficiency advantages, state-of-the-art denoising, and the reported 42× latency and 149× energy advantages. The abstract is shortened, but the additional experiments support rather than redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains that Loihi batching trades increased silicon resources for throughput and is practical only for small models and batches. It also qualifies the keyword-spotting result: larger sparse models are needed to compare at the higher accuracies reached by dense models. Existing quantization and GPU-comparison limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SparseRNNs code-access link and specifies model replication and the 16-chip VPX hardware for batching. Section 2.2 revises the stated Loihi I/O capacity from 160 million to 26 million 32-bit messages per second. Existing software versions and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Voelker et al. (2019) and Chilkuri et al. (2021) on Legendre memory units, while removing Gu et al. (2021) and Gu and Dao (2023) from the cited background and references. This adjusts historical attribution without substantially changing novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, locally edits the introduction and technical prose, and formats the research questions as a numbered list. Author Contributions is removed, while Acknowledgments and an Impact Statement are added. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds batching and keyword-spotting plots, relocates Figure 5, renumbers retained appendix figures, and updates diagram labels and Figure 6's caption. Table 1 retains its structure. New Figure 9 incorrectly labels its accuracy axis as 'Test SI-SNR (dB)', creating a localized presentation defect.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 broadens empirical support through keyword spotting and provides useful evidence about small-batch deployment, including its silicon-resource limitation. The code-access link also improves reproducibility information. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the keyword-spotting experiment and Figure 9's incorrect metric label; the established central results remain unchanged.
